cards.text: Right before this, God's people heard comfort, and a picture of God as a shepherd carrying His lambs close to His heart (Isaiah 40:1, 11). Now the prophet starts asking questions. BIG ones: “Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or marked off the heavens with the span of his hand?”

cards.question: The prophet keeps going. Who has weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills with a balance? Who is he pointing to?

cards.text: Then the prophet asks, “Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or informed Him as His counselor?” Picture somebody walking up to God with a clipboard. “Small note, LORD. The mountains? Little heavy.”

cards.question: The prophet says God once needed someone to teach Him the paths of justice and the way of understanding.

cards.text: Now the prophet turns to the nations. Empires, armies, kings with big crowns, the whole lineup.

cards.question: How does the prophet say the nations look next to God?

answers.text: Like a drop in a bucket

cards.text: Then the prophet points to Lebanon, a land known for its cedar trees (1 Kings 5:6). Picture every tree as fuel and every animal on the altar for one burnt offering.

cards.question: All of Lebanon's wood and animals together would be enough for a burnt offering to God.
The prophet sums up the nations: all the nations are as ___ before Him.

cards.text: So the prophet asks it straight: “To whom will you liken God? To what image will you compare Him?” Go ahead, friend. Name something.
He brings up an idol. A craftsman casts it, and a metalworker covers it in gold and fits it with silver chains.

cards.question: Not everyone can afford gold. What does someone without that kind of offering choose to make his idol from?
He also looks for a skilled craftsman to set up the idol so it will not topple.

cards.text: A god you have to keep from tipping over. Friend, I stand on a gold base too, and PLEASE don't pray to me. Then the prophet turns to the people: “Do you not know? Have you not heard?”

cards.question: The prophet says where God really sits. Where is He enthroned?

answers.text: Above the circle of the earth

cards.question: From where God sits, the earth's dwellers are like ___.

cards.text: And the sky? “He stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.” Friend, it takes me three hops and a prayer just to hang up my apron.

cards.question: God brings the princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth meaningless.

cards.text: Then a picture from the field. The rulers are like plants: no sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, no sooner have their stems taken root in the ground…

cards.question: When God blows on the rulers, they ___.

cards.text: Remember the question about who God compares to? Now the Holy One asks it Himself: “To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?”
Then the prophet says, “Lift up your eyes on high: Who created all these?” He's pointing at the stars.

cards.question: The prophet says God leads out the starry host by number. What does He do for each star?

answers.text: He calls each one by name
He gives each one a season
He hides each one by day

cards.question: Because of God's great power and mighty strength, not one of the stars is missing.

cards.text: Every star, by NAME. Friend, I've got stars lighting up over my bakery one sealed cookie box at a time, and I lose count before my second batch.
Now the prophet speaks to God's people as Jacob and Israel, after their forefather Jacob, whom God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28). And they've got a complaint.

cards.question: What are Jacob and Israel saying about the LORD?

answers.text: Their way is hidden from Him
He is angry with them forever

cards.text: God calls every star by name, and they think He lost track of THEM? I get it, friend. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer sure the whole world forgot me.
The prophet comes right back: “Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth.”

cards.question: The prophet says the everlasting God will grow tired and weary.
What does the prophet say about the LORD's understanding?

answers.text: No one can search it out
Only the priests can learn it

cards.question: The LORD gives power to the ___ and increases the strength of the weak.

cards.text: Then the prophet says, “Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.” If young men stumble, there's hope for a stamper who trips over his own mustache.

cards.question: Everybody gets tired. So who does the prophet say will renew their strength?

answers.text: Those who wait upon the LORD

cards.question: Those who wait upon the LORD will mount up with wings like ___.
Those who wait upon the LORD will run and not grow weary, and they will walk and not faint.

cards.text: Run and not grow weary. Friend, I get winded hopping from oven two to oven three, so I'm holding on to THAT one.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote of 40:13, the clipboard setup, and the standalone made-up line "Small note, LORD. The mountains? Little heavy."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "So the prophet asks it straight: …", "Go ahead, friend." and "Name something."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question opens with "He also looks for…". "He" points back to the man from the previous choice card, which is no longer on screen. The question should say who, for example "The man making a wooden idol also looks for…".

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "A god you have to keep from tipping over.", the gold-base joke, and "Then the prophet turns to the people: …"

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "And the sky?", the standalone quote of 40:22, and the apron joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card gives 40:26 to the prophet ("Then the prophet says"). This line comes right after the Holy One speaks in 40:25, and the text doesn't say whether the Holy One is still speaking or the prophet has picked up again. The card should leave the speaker open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the star contrast, "I get it, friend." and the junk drawer line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card states that God calls every star by name, which is 40:26, but it cites only Isaiah 40:27. The citation should be Isaiah 40:26-27.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question begins "Everybody gets tired." Verse 30 says even youths grow tired and weary, but verse 31 says those who wait upon the LORD will run and not grow weary. "Everybody" stretches the text past what it says.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Those who wait upon the LORD", is the only one that sounds like the Bible or mentions the LORD. "Those who train the hardest" sounds like modern gym talk. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
